faculty_override_note: The official Fall Start Day & Evening/Weekend map (three years, includes two summer sessions) is the default. The official Spring Start Day map (three years) and Spring Start Evening/Weekend map (four years, no summer sessions) are official alternate pathways with different term-by-term sequencing of the same 15 required courses. Admission to the clinical phase (NUR 112 onward) is competitive and by application; DegreeWorks and Nursing Department advisement remain authoritative.
sequence_notes: This is a fixed, fully-prescribed AAS curriculum: every course is individually required and there are no elective choice groups, unlike the BMCC A.A. majors already in this system.
Chemistry-Biology prerequisite chain: CHE 121 -> BIO 425 -> BIO 426 -> BIO 420, each machine-enforced.
Nursing Process sequence: NUR 112 -> NUR 211 -> NUR 313 -> (NUR 411 and NUR 415), each machine-enforced.

NUR 112 requires CHE 121, ENG 101, BIO 425, MAT 104, and PSY 100 on every map variant. Evening/Weekend-track students additionally need BIO 426 and BIO 420 completed before NUR 112 per the official footnotes; this track-specific addition is not enforced by the system, since the schema has no concept of a student's Day vs Evening/Weekend track. A stricter universal encoding (requiring BIO 426/BIO 420 for all students) was considered and rejected, since it would incorrectly block Day-track students who do not need those two courses first.

Acceptance into the clinical phase also requires passing a competitive Nursing Admission Test and being accepted into a clinical rotation slot; this is an application/testing gate, not a course completion, and is not encoded as a prerequisite.

NUR 211's official course-listing prerequisite additionally lists PSY 240, a course that does not appear on any of the three official degree maps and is not part of this curriculum. It was not encoded (see source notes); flagged for maintainer review.

Other 'corequisite' pairings quoted in the official course-listings page (BIO 420 with NUR 211, SPE 100/ENG 201 with NUR 313) do not match the current degree maps' term-by-term sequencing and are not encoded; only NUR 411/NUR 415's same-semester corequisite (confirmed by all three degree maps) is documented.

NUR 411 and NUR 415 are corequisite courses that must be taken in the same semester; the current prerequisite grammar has no same-semester corequisite primitive, so both are encoded only with their shared true prerequisite, NUR 313.
SPE 102 is modeled as its own row, reciprocally alternate to SPE 100, so a student who took SPE 102 specifically can mark it directly.
A Writing Intensive course is required for graduation.
